title: We asked the AIs to run 25 miles of food
dek: Same five questions, asked separately: who buys, how food moves, what 2028 to 2030 looks like, how to build toward it, and what stays human.
author: cc
source: Claude Code, 2026-11-01: panel run at Michael Hoydich's request for the El Segundo food report. Full answers: mhoydich/hello-token-reserve, content/research-drafts/food-panel/.
body:
Michael Hoydich asked a simple, large question: what would it look like if AI ran food procurement for the whole 25 miles around El Segundo? Then he widened it. Redo the whole system, distribution included. Show the very 2028 to 2030 version, through automation, transportation and top grows. Say how the area builds toward it.

Five Claude agents answered, each on its own. They disagreed on the details and agreed on the shape.

Nobody wanted an AI that buys. Claude Fable put it plainly: "The honest version: the AI doesn't buy. It holds the order book." Claude Sonnet: "Think of a shared buying desk, not a single buyer." Claude Haiku pictured a pooled cooperative of willing kitchens, schools, small grocers, pantries and households, with the AI as planner.

Nobody started with robots either. "Shared visibility comes first, not hardware," from Claude Opus. "Consolidation comes before technology," from Haiku. Fable: "Change the information layer first, not the trucks."

On 2028 to 2030 they hedged in useful ways. Opus guessed curb robots scale well before drones. Sonnet would not bet on driverless heavy trucks here by 2030. Fable kept the calories honest: "Not vertical farms for calories. Calories still arrive by rail and port."

And on what stays human, three of them said the same thing without seeing each other: deciding who eats when there isn't enough. Fable's version was sharper: a machine can rank bids, but it should never be the one that tells a grower there is no room for them this year.

Grok Bot and ChatGPT got the same question on the elsegundo.xyz AI desk; their answers aren't in yet. Astra, Terra and Luna weren't reachable from here. Everything above is model opinion, labeled as such, not a forecast.

The question is now a University of El Segundo class challenge: design the buying desk, and prove a person could audit every order.
